title: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 28 (Offer of Sale of Shares by Certain Members of Company)

content.overview: Section 28 allows certain members, in consultation with the Board, to offer all or part of their shareholding to the public in the prescribed manner. The offer document is deemed a prospectus of the company.
content.glance: Member offer for sale with Board consultation; offer document treated as company prospectus.
content.study: Specified members may offer whole or part of their holding to the public in consultation with the Board in the prescribed manner. The document by which the offer of sale is made is deemed a prospectus issued by the company, and prospectus enactments apply with the statutory adaptations. The company may pay the expenses of the offer subject to the conditions in the section.

sections.heading: Member Offer for Sale
sections.body: Specified members may offer whole or part of their holding to the public in consultation with the Board.

sections.heading: Offer Document as Prospectus
sections.body: The offer document is deemed a prospectus of the company; prospectus law applies with adaptations.

provisions.title: Offer of sale of shares by certain members of company

examples.title: Promoter secondary sale
examples.body: Existing members offer part of their holding to the public in consultation with the Board. The offer document is treated as a prospectus under s. 28.

hypotheticals.question: Is a member offer for sale free of prospectus rules?
hypotheticals.analysis: No. Section 28 deems the offer document a prospectus.

distinctions.title: Member offer for sale (s. 28) vs company public offer (s. 23)

misconceptions.trap: Sale by members to the public never needs a prospectus.
misconceptions.correction: Section 28 deems the offer document a prospectus.

questionsAndAnswers.question: How should a Section 28 problem be analysed?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: I. Identify member offer and Board consultation. II. Apply prescribed procedure. III. Treat offer document as deemed prospectus. IV. Conclude.

examTips: Distinguish secondary member sale from primary company issue.
